races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: Hold-up juvenile who has yet to win or place over distances beyond 8f, with all six career runs coming at shorter; the step to 1m4f on quick ground is an unproven stamina question, and Charlie Fellowes' 14-day strike rate of 1/19 does not inspire confidence, though he does arrive with a recent run under his belt 21 days ago.

runners_data.name: Zurna
runners_data.note: Shaped best in her most recent run, finishing second over 10f on good ground — the most relevant piece of form in this field for today's trip and conditions — and Dylan Hogan's booking is a positive; a natural hold-up type who needs Darkest Red to come back to her, but the trip and going combination gives her a genuine shout.

runners_data.name: Celestarak
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Epsom in the past, which is a significant course and distance tick, but David Menuisier's runner arrives as a true hold-up type pushed onto the pace map in midfield due to redistribution — his tendency to fade in the finish is a concern on quick ground if the pace is steady and the race does not truly test stamina; style fit is discounted accordingly.

runners_data.name: Society Girl
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has been off 59 days and her recent form shows a string of disappointing efforts including a tenth over 12f on good ground — the layoff and regressive form make her a significant watch-and-wait proposition; she is a natural closer whose redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded hold-up end of this field, and her chance depends on a truly run race that does not materialise here.

runners_data.name: Darkest Red
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's consistent front-runner has hit the frame in four of her last five starts and clearly loves front-running at 1m2f-1m4f on good ground; Callum Hutchinson takes over in the saddle, the style-fit tag reflects that her best form has come when allowed to dominate, and with no pace rival in sight today that scenario is squarely on the cards.

races.paceDynamic: Darkest Red is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should control matters from the front at whatever tempo suits connections over 1m4f on good-to-firm ground at Epsom. With Celestarak, Society Girl, Zurna, and Tai Hang Pegasus all naturally inclined to race in the rear half, Darkest Red faces no meaningful pressure and can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop that plays directly into her stamina profile and her series of placed efforts at longer trips. The four hold-up types — three of whom are redistributed onto the pace map because the field contains more closers than the diagram can accommodate at the rear — will be reliant on Darkest Red either going hard enough to come back to them or the Epsom undulations stretching the field in the straight. The race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile, with Darkest Red able to control tempo and Zurna and Celestarak, the two hold-up horses with the most relevant form at today's trip and going, the most credible challengers if they find enough late ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Darkest Red Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Darkest Red breaks cleanly and sets a measured, uncontested gallop, exploiting the absence of any pace rival.
scenarios.body: Darkest Red dictates every yard at a tempo that suits her stamina, reaching the Epsom straight with her field spread out behind and enough in reserve to resist late challengers. This shape rewards the prominent/lead profile above all, and Darkest Red's consistent placed runs at 1m2f-1m4f on good ground support her holding on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Darkest Red sets a stronger pace than intended, leaving herself vulnerable to a sustained late rally from the closers.
scenarios.body: The undulations of Epsom stretch the field in the straight, and a hold-up horse with the stamina to see out 1m4f on quick ground picks up the pieces late. Zurna's recent placed effort over 10f on good ground and Celestarak's Epsom win give both credibility in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the race turns into a sprint finish in the straight, favouring a horse with tactical speed from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over Epsom's unique contours can compress the field and make tactical speed decisive from the two-furlong pole. Tai Hang Pegasus or Society Girl, operating closer to the pace than their natural style dictates in this compressed scenario, could find themselves in the right place at the right time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If there is trouble in running, a significant stumble on the camber, or Darkest Red is slowly away and the field bunches with no clear pace.
scenarios.body: Without Darkest Red establishing control, the race loses its shape entirely and becomes a scrambling affair decided on luck in running. Any runner could theoretically benefit, but this is a low-probability scenario in a well-ordered five-horse field on a clear surface.

watchPoints.text: Darkest Red's ability to break cleanly and immediately establish the lead is the single most important factor in this race — if she is slow into stride, the entire pace map collapses.
Celestarak's Epsom course win is eye-catching but her tendency to fade in the finish, combined with a steady tempo set by Darkest Red, could mean her historical form flatters her chance here today.
Society Girl's 59-day absence is the longest layoff in this field — monitor market moves at the off to gauge whether Ed Walker has her fit enough to perform after this break.

Zurna's second-place finish over 10f on good ground is the standout piece of running-style-friendly form for a hold-up horse in this race — watch how quickly Dylan Hogan can position her to challenge entering the straight.

With four hold-up types and one front-runner, the Epsom camber and descent into Tattenham Corner could cause significant bunching among the closers — watch for any interference or checking in the early stages that disrupts the hold-up runners' rhythm.

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Robert Dyas Partnership Handicap

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with three placings at seven furlongs including two on good, handled by a capable claimer in Muscutt; needs a proper gallop to close into and the small six-runner field limits traffic problems, but three wins of zero from 22 career starts raises questions about a finishing effort when it matters.

runners_data.name: Stenmark
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed front-runner with Rhys Clutterbuck in the saddle; OR 75 and four runs on similar going with two places, but the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 reflects that he is being asked to operate from a slightly more prominent position than his norm — if he settles and controls the fractions, the race is his to lose.

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 5-year-old carries headgear and has one win at seven furlongs on similar going from 15 attempts; trainer is 6/35 in the 14-day window which is modest but active, and a naturally prominent style gives her a good view of proceedings behind Stenmark.

runners_data.name: Panelli
runners_data.note: Neil Callan rides a horse returning from a 147-day absence, which is the single biggest concern — two placed efforts at seven and eight furlongs on standard suggest ability, but Stuart Williams has one winner from 18 in his 14-day form and the hold-up style needs a race run honestly to deliver.

runners_data.name: Jersey Maverick
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes has been finding winners (1/18 in the 14-day window) and Jersey Maverick has twice placed at seven furlongs on good ground including a recent runner-up over six at Goodwood; a natural front-runner by inclination, he has been pushed back to a midfield mapping because the race has one too many prominent types for him to operate from his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle is in decent form (1/4 in 14 days) and this horse won at seven furlongs on standard ground last time out, but 97 days off the track and an OR drop to 62 raises durability questions; another horse whose front-running tendency has been displaced by Stenmark's dominance of the early pace, leaving him to travel in an unnatural position.

races.paceDynamic: Stenmark is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival pressing from the gates, should secure a comfortable lead through the early furlongs on Good to Firm ground at Epsom. The pace he sets will be measured rather than scorching — a solo lead on a flat seven furlongs creates a rhythm that suits the horse dictating terms rather than those chasing. Jersey Maverick and Dandy Khan are both natural prominent types but this field holds more horses who want to race up with the pace than the race shape can accommodate — Stenmark is most likely to claim the rail position, with Jersey Maverick marginally better placed than Dandy Khan to secure cover just behind. A controlled, single-paced contest that does not fall apart at the two-furlong pole strongly favours prominent and lead profiles, particularly Stenmark if he settles cleanly, while the genuine hold-up horses Potomac River and Panelli face the challenge of closing on a well-rated gallop with limited sectional pressure to open up the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stenmark Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Stenmark jumps cleanly and secures an uncontested lead, setting an honest but unforced tempo on good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: Stenmark dictates from the front with Rhys Clutterbuck able to manage the fractions on a flat Epsom seven furlongs, making every yard and presenting a clear target that this small field struggles to overhaul. Prominent types who tuck in behind benefit most from the rhythm, and Silver Trumpet's hold on a prominent position gives her the best chance of picking up the pieces if Stenmark fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Stenmark's early dominance is eroded in the final two furlongs and a prominent mover delivers a late kick.
scenarios.body: Jersey Maverick has the form figures to suggest she can travel powerfully in a small field and, if she secures a handy position just off Stenmark, can challenge inside the final furlong on ground that suits her. Dandy Khan, off a 97-day break but with a trainer who has been active recently, is capable of grabbing a share if the front-runner's effort fades.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and the late runners find a clear run in a small six-runner field.
scenarios.body: Potomac River has placed twice at seven furlongs on good ground and, with Daniel Muscutt finding a clean passage, could rattle home if an honest gallop opens up space through the final quarter-mile. Panelli is 147 days off the track and has placed twice at seven and eight furlongs but the long layoff makes this scenario speculative even if the race shape were to suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Stenmark mis-jumps or is crowded early and the pace collapses, turning it into a scrappy sprint home with no clear flow.
scenarios.body: Without a dominant pace-setter getting away cleanly, the race loses its structure entirely, and a horse with fresh legs and tactical flexibility could pinch it in the confusion. Panelli's sharp form earlier in the year and Potomac River's consistency at this trip mean either could benefit from a scrambled finish, though this shape is the least probable given Stenmark's clear advantage at the front.

watchPoints.text: Stenmark's jump and first furlong — if he is outpaced or crowded at the start, the entire race shape collapses and the scenario probabilities shift dramatically toward hold-up horses.

Jersey Maverick and Dandy Khan are both natural front-runners squeezed into prominent/midfield roles — watch for early jostling between them in the first two furlongs as both riders look for their natural position.
Panelli's fitness after 147 days off the track is the biggest unknown in the field — if Neil Callan asks for early effort to compensate, the horse's hold-up profile becomes even more compromised.

Good to Firm ground at Epsom favours consistent, honest galloping types over late finishers — Potomac River's closing style has placed on this surface but never won, which is relevant if Stenmark produces a clean lead-and-hold performance.

races.name: Robert Dyas Handicap

runners_data.name: Aberama Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent sprint handicapper who won over course and distance on good ground, but needs to come from well off the pace — nine-year-old wearing a visor, handled by David O'Meara's useful Daniel Muscutt, and similar-going form reads only one win from fifteen comparable starts; back in 19 days, competitive but positionally reliant on a strong pace.|

runners_data.name: Rage Of Thunder
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner who should stride straight to the front and set his own terms; recent course win over this trip on good ground is a strong positive, but trainer Gary & Josh Moore's 14-day strike rate of 4/29 is modest and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is not a concern here as he is squarely in his natural role.|

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance on good going and shaped well last time when second over course and distance in similar conditions, giving him the most relevant form in the race; Michael Attwater's yard is cold (0/9 over 14 days) and Paddy Bradley is a light-weight claimer, but the profile of a horse who travels prominently on fast ground is ideally suited to this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer back on preferred good/firm turf after a break of just five days, which is a tight turnaround; George Scott's 2/13 14-day record is modest and a headgear flag (p) suggests the yard is searching for improvement, but course and distance form reading 4th and 2nd on good-to-soft is encouraging if the ground rides on the quicker side.|

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on standard ground last time out and the form reads better than his current OR of 72 suggests; true hold-up horse who needs to close from off the pace, and similar-going stats (0 wins, 2 places from 5 comparable runs) temper enthusiasm, though Dylan Cunha's horse is unexposed at this level and carries a light weight.|

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: Veteran sprint handicapper whose last five runs show a string of double-figure finishes — form is deeply worrying regardless of tactics; genuinely races from the rear but with more closers than the shape can handle, he is further compromised positionally, and STYLE_FIT (0.92) underlines that this shape offers him very little.|

runners_data.name: Balon D'or
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's five-year-old has shown only limited ability in recent starts, all on the all-weather at Lingfield/Kempton; a natural hold-up horse whose turf and grass sprint form is sparse and unimpressive — the 35-day absence and cold trainer record (0/5) add further caution, and being forced to race in midfield rather than from his natural position compounds the difficulty.|

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: Showed ability to win over 5f on good ground and recorded a placed run over today's trip, so the raw form is not without merit; Peter Crate's low 14-day volume (0/1) limits confidence in stable readiness, and the horse's natural tendency to race from behind — reflected in the redistribution note — means his best chance requires a pace scenario this race is unlikely to produce.|

races.paceDynamic: Rage Of Thunder is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, will control this race from the front at a sustainable tempo over Epsom's straight six. Twirler and Acclaimed Freedom will look to press from prominent positions just behind, but neither is a true front-runner and neither is likely to force Rage Of Thunder into a punishing early battle. The resulting shape is a single-file, controlled gallop with a moderate-to-honest pace that rewards horses who can travel close to the action and quicken off the steady fractions — this race shape clearly favours prominent and on-pace runners over genuine hold-up types. Ancient Times, Balon D'or, and Harry Brown are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more rear-of-field types than the shape can accommodate at the back, meaning none of them are likely to secure their natural position or benefit from a late run on a track that offers little back-straight cover.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rage Of Thunder Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rage Of Thunder dictates from flag to finish at a comfortable tempo and no rival has the pace to challenge early.
scenarios.body: Rage Of Thunder sets a measured pace on the Epsom straight, the field strings out and those racing prominently hold their positions as the fractions stay honest rather than punishing; horses who can track the leader within two lengths have a decisive positional advantage entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: On-Pace Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Twirler or Acclaimed Freedom travels prominently and accelerates past a tiring Rage Of Thunder inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A controlled front-end gallop allows prominent horses to cover their ground without burning reserves, and the two-furlong dip at Epsom tests a lone front-runner's stamina late; Twirler's proven course-and-distance winning form on good ground makes this the most plausible challenge to the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a hold-up horse finds a clear run through.
scenarios.body: Aberama Gold has proven she can finish strongly on good ground at this course and distance, and King Of Chaos recorded a recent win over course and distance that suggests raw ability; however the lack of genuine pace and the redistribution of the true hold-up horses to midfield means a late run requires both a strong pace collapse and a clean passage — both unlikely in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Falls Apart Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Rage Of Thunder fails to see out the trip and the race becomes a scramble from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With the field tightly compressed and several out-of-role hold-up types forced to race prominently, any pace collapse could trigger an untidy finish where the horse with the freshest legs in the final 100 yards prevails; King Of Chaos and Aberama Gold, carrying lighter weights, have the residual class and recent winning form to capitalise on a chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Rage Of Thunder's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest determinant of the race outcome — if anything forces him to go faster than comfortable in the first two furlongs, every scenario probability shifts markedly toward on-pace or hold-up challengers.|

Twirler's jockey Paddy Bradley is relatively inexperienced at this level; watch for him to be positioned correctly within two lengths of Rage Of Thunder from the break, as any loss of ground early on Epsom's short-run six furlongs will cost him the race.|

Acclaimed Freedom's five-day turnaround warrants monitoring in pre-race — if the yard shows any signs of training-related concern or the horse appears flat in the paddock, his prominent-race profile becomes significantly less reliable.|

Ancient Times, Balon D'or, and Harry Brown are all natural closers forced into midfield by the field's composition — watch to see if any of them drift back toward their natural position early, as that would effectively remove them from contention on a straight six with no pace collapse expected.|

The going is reported as Good to Firm for this race despite the headline card showing Good — horses with any going concern on faster ground, particularly Acclaimed Freedom (hg:p), should be assessed at the start for any signs of unease.|

races.name: Betfred 'Nifty 50' Handicap

runners_data.name: Happy Banner
runners_data.note: Flagged STYLE_FIT (0.93) as this prominent type is effectively being asked to lead, which tempers confidence; Ed Walker sends it here 12 days after its last run carrying 142lbs and holds course-similar going form (six runs at the trip/going, three placed), but the weight burden and role stretch are genuine concerns.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's hold-up specialist arrives 10 days fresh, won last time at 7f on Good, and bumps up to 8f here; sim-going record of 6 runs with one win and one place suggests it handles the surface, but the step up in trip and Epsom's unique demands put a question over whether a horse that likes to come late can generate momentum up the final hill.

runners_data.name: Darvel
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with genuine hold-up instincts, Patrick Chamings sends him here 18 days after his last run; his recent form string of -95002 is modest and his sim-going figures (8 from 15, two wins five places) reflect experience rather than brilliance — he holds this sort of ground well, but the redistribution note means he may not get the deep cover he needs to produce his best.

runners_data.name: Prodigal Son
runners_data.note: Heather Main's four-year-old steps back to 8f after a winning run at that trip, though the 39-day absence and Main's 0/5 trainer-14 record is a flag; naturally a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position, his true closer's profile means he needs a strong pace he may not get here, and the 0/10 sim-going record makes this surface a question mark.

runners_data.name: Buy The Dip
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle has this six-year-old back quickly (9 days), and his sim-going record of 10 from 15 (one win, four places) shows genuine comfort on this surface; by nature a hold-up horse placed in midfield by redistribution, his best efforts have come when there's a real gallop to close into — the moderate pace expected here is the critical risk to his chance.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: The other Boyle runner, this four-year-old is a genuine prominent type with solid sim-going credentials (12 from 15, two wins six places) and won at 8f on Good; Donagh Murphy (7) takes the ride after 30 days off, and Play Me is one of the best-profile horses for the likely race shape — though the amateur claim and absence are minor queries.

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old carries the visor and has the joint-highest OR (72) in the field; four runs at this trip/going type (five from six sim, one win two places) underline suitability, and a genuine prominent style means Rhys Clutterbuck can slot in just behind the leader — this profile looks naturally aligned with how this race should unfold.

runners_data.name: Ritaal
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick's three-year-old is the lightest in the weights (128lbs) and holds a tongue-tie/blinkers headgear note; 35 days since last run, all his recent starts have come on Standard (AW) which raises a legitimate concern about handling Good to Firm turf, and the hold-up style may leave him with too much to do at Epsom against more experienced rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Happy Banner is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over this 1m½f trip at Epsom. Swiped and Play Me are the two genuine prominent racers who will look to track Happy Banner in the first two or three positions, giving the race a tidy, unhurried complexion unless one of them decides to press from flagfall. The field contains more hold-up types than Epsom's unique downhill-then-uphill configuration can comfortably accommodate — Prodigal Son, Darvel, and Buy The Dip are all natural off-the-pace horses mapped to midfield, but they are unlikely to fully reclaim their preferred rear-of-field position given the field dynamics. With one horse controlling a manageable pace and prominent racers poised just behind, this race shape strongly favours horses that can sit prominently and quicken through the final two furlongs, rather than late closers who need a truly searching gallop to reel them in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Banner dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and prominent chasers exploit the clean ground ahead of them.
scenarios.body: Happy Banner sets a rhythm that suits horses sitting just off the pace, with Swiped and Play Me ideally placed to pounce as the track turns uphill in the final furlong; this scenario rewards horses that travel prominently and quicken rather than those making up ground from the back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Ups Land
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Banner sets an unsustainably quick early tempo and ties up in the final furlong, leaving a gap for late arrivals.
scenarios.body: A hot early pace would string the field out along Epsom's descent and create a genuine closing opportunity in the last two furlongs for horses with a late kick; however, this depends on conditions that look unlikely given Happy Banner's expected moderate front-running style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Scramble, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If early pace is deliberately steadied to a crawl and the race turns into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A bunched field would make the race a lottery on the straight, with horses breaking from midfield having as much chance as any leader; Prodigal Son and Buy The Dip would need to find clear daylight quickly, which Epsom's tight finish doesn't always grant.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Banner is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the prominent chasers fail to reel it in under weight.
scenarios.body: An untroubled Happy Banner could steal a march and simply outstay rivals on good to firm ground if its nearest rivals miss the break or get detached; this is a lower-probability outcome given Happy Banner's style-fit flag suggesting it may not fully relish the front-running role.

watchPoints.text: Happy Banner's weight (142lbs) combined with the STYLE_FIT flag means if it ties up on the hill the race opens up dramatically — watch how comfortably it's travelling entering the final two furlongs.

Swiped's visor is worth noting as it has been worn before and the horse is prominent-minded — if it over-races chasing Happy Banner down the Epsom descent, it could burn its finish before the uphill run home.

Prodigal Son and Buy The Dip are both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield positions; if either jockey tries to force their natural position and ends up at the rear, they face Epsom's notoriously unforgiving closing straight with too much to do.
Play Me's 30-day absence for Jim Boyle (trainer 14-day record 1/16) is worth monitoring — if it shows any signs of needing the run it may be outpaced at a crucial stage by the fresher Swiped.

Ritaal's entire recent form coming on AW Standard surfaces means this Good to Firm turf conditions is an unknown quantity — watch the betting market for any sign the team has concerns, or conversely confidence if supported.

races.name: Betfred Play Fred's 5 Million Pound Handicap

runners_data.name: Living In Hope
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Harry Eustace stepping up in trip from 8f; three-year-old with modest recent form (0-5-4) but the extra furlong at Epsom could unlock improvement, and 34 days since last run is a routine freshen-up rather than a concern.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 8f on good and standard ground this season and is the lone confirmed pace-setter; Paddy Bradley must dictate cleanly from the gates — if that goes to plan the style fit at this trip on fast ground is compelling despite the STYLE_FIT tag reflecting it racing outside its narrowest role.

runners_data.name: Don Pablo Colina
runners_data.note: George Baker's three-year-old has run three times without threatening the frame; Neil Callan takes over but the form reads 5-6-8 and there is little in the data to suggest a step forward on Good to Firm at Epsom.

runners_data.name: Minerality
runners_data.note: Dr Newland & Insole's hold-up type carries a noted finishing fade flag, which is a significant liability in a slowly-run race over 1m2f; form of 8-9-6 offers little encouragement even if the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/28 hints at some activity in the yard.

runners_data.name: Sweep In Time
runners_data.note: 190 days off the track is an immediate concern for this two-year-old; a genuine deep hold-up type by inclination, the compact field means it is unlikely to get into its natural position at the rear, and the redistribution into midfield reduces its effectiveness — Tom Clover's yard has only one recent runner at this meet.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: The most consistently placed horse in the race, with two second-place finishes in its last four starts; apprentice Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) helps offset the weight, and the headgear note (p) alongside a sharp 17-day turnaround from a second at 8f on good suggest Jonathan Portman has this horse fit and primed for a prominent challenge.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's three-year-old has a finishing fade flag and a form line of 0-4-8; sim-going figures show a placing at 3 runs but the Epsom camber and fast ground are demanding, and as a redistributed hold-up type mapped to midfield it faces a structural disadvantage against a slow pace.

races.paceDynamic: Sail On Sailor is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger to the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Epsom's 1m2f on Good to Firm ground. Takeitorleaveit is the only other prominent-minded horse in the field and will likely sit just off the pace in second or third, meaning Sail On Sailor faces no serious pressure early and can set a rhythm entirely on its own terms. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Sweep In Time and Cormorant Rock are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield, but they are unlikely to secure that deep position in a race where the pace is modest and the field is compact at seven runners. A controlled, front-running tempo on fast ground at Epsom — where the undulations and camber suit front-runners who travel well through the race — strongly favours horses that can race prominently and sustain their effort, disadvantaging true hold-up types who need a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sail On Sailor Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Sail On Sailor secures an uncontested lead and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Sail On Sailor controls every yard, conserving energy on the long run to Tattenham Corner before lengthening on the straight; a comfortable tempo starves the hold-up horses of the strong pace they need to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit tracks Sail On Sailor closely and pounces in the final two furlongs as the leader tires.
scenarios.body: Takeitorleaveit's recent form shows consistent placing from prominent positions and it is well-weighted on OR 58; if Sail On Sailor sets only a modest tempo, Takeitorleaveit can use its finishing kick at the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Sail On Sailor sets a stronger-than-expected pace that strings the field out and creates enough of a gap for a midfield mover.
scenarios.body: Living In Hope, racing from hold-up to midfield, is the best-credentialed closer here and could benefit if the pace genuinely quickens; this scenario requires a genuine galop that the current race shape does not obviously project.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the straight and a fresh-legged hold-up horse finishes fastest of all.
scenarios.body: Sweep In Time and Cormorant Rock are the deepest hold-up types but both carry redistribution caveats — neither is likely to be positioned far enough back to deliver a true late run, and both carry fade flags; this is the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sail On Sailor must break cleanly — if it misses the kick and Takeitorleaveit hits the front instead, the entire pace map inverts and the race dynamic changes fundamentally.

Takeitorleaveit wears headgear and returns just 17 days after its last run — watch for it travelling conspicuously well just off the pace in the first half-mile, as Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim makes it a live danger if Sail On Sailor weakens early in the straight.

Sweep In Time is 190 days absent and is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by the race shape — monitor its behaviour in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of rustiness that could see it detached before the home turn.

Living In Hope is the best-credentialed finisher but needs a stronger gallop than Sail On Sailor is likely to set; watch whether Callum Hutchinson moves early to compensate, which would tell you the horse is not getting the run of the race it needs.

Cormorant Rock carries a finishing fade flag on Good to Firm and is rated OR 45 — if it is prominent early against its natural inclination, that is a sign the redistribution has worked against its chance entirely.
